subject: Art & Design
source: National Curriculum (Art and Design). Drive Art & Design folder reviewed (Elements of Art deck, KS3 files) and the school's 'Art - Y9' lesson plan example used for format and the Y9 Zentangle topic.

lessons.title: Colour hunt: finding and naming colours
objectives: Find and draw colours from around the home
Mix two colours by layering crayons

keywords.def: what we see when light bounces off things, like red or blue
three main colours we can use to make other colours
to put one colour on top of another

starter: Bismillah. Hold up something red. What colour is it?
Can you name three colours you can see in the room?
What colour is the sky today?

teach.heading: Bismillah and our colourful world
bullets: Allah made a world full of colours
Look at flowers, leaves and the sky
Say thank you to Allah for what we see
teach.note: Say bismillah together. Pupils need paper and 3 crayons (red, yellow, blue). Show a leaf or flower on camera and ask what colours the children can name. Praise every answer.

teach.heading: Naming colours
bullets: Red, yellow and blue are main colours
Green is the colour of leaves
Orange is the colour of an orange
teach.note: Hold up each crayon slowly. Children call out the name. Common mistake: mixing up green and blue; repeat with objects.

teach.heading: Mixing by layering
bullets: Colour red, then colour yellow on top
Red and yellow make orange
Yellow and blue make green
teach.note: Model colouring lightly. Ask 'What do you think will happen?' before each layer. Press softly so both colours show.

teach.heading: Colour hunt
bullets: Find something red at home
Find something yellow
Draw it and colour it in
teach.note: Give 2 minutes for pupils to fetch an item and show the camera. Remind them to walk and ask a grown-up first.

practice: Show me something red from your home.
Colour a circle yellow, then put blue on top. What colour do you get?
independent: Draw three objects from the colour hunt. Colour each one carefully.
Make a rainbow of five stripes using all the colours you know.
exit: Name one thing that is orange.
lessons.homework: Find three yellow things at home and tell a grown-up their names.
lessons.send: SEND: give two crayons only and one stripe at a time; EAL: say colour names with the object; stretch: mix a third colour by layering and name it.

lessons.title: Pattern makers: shapes that repeat
objectives: Make a repeating pattern with shapes and colours

keywords.def: shapes or colours that repeat again and again
to do the same thing again
three shapes we can use for patterns

starter: Bismillah. What colours did you find last time?
Name a shape you can see in the room.
Clap this pattern back: clap, clap, stamp.

teach.heading: Patterns in our world
bullets: A pattern repeats again and again
Look at tiles, curtains and carpets
Mosque tiles often use beautiful patterns
teach.note: Show a picture or a real tiled surface or patterned cloth. Ask: what do you see again and again? Avoid pictures of people; use tiles, stripes, fabrics.

teach.heading: A, B, A, B pattern
bullets: Circle, square, circle, square
Red, blue, red, blue
What comes next?
teach.note: Draw on a board or paper. Let children predict the next shape. Misconception: a pattern needs a repeat, not just any shapes in a row.

teach.heading: Making our own pattern
bullets: Choose two shapes and two colours
Draw them in a row
Keep going to the end of the page
teach.note: Model drawing a row slowly. Tell them crayons only; no scissors needed. Walk through the row with them.

teach.heading: Show and share
bullets: Hold your pattern to the camera
Tell us the pattern
Say Alhamdulillah for your work
teach.note: Invite 4 or 5 children to say their pattern aloud, e.g. 'circle, triangle, circle, triangle'.

practice: Say the next shape: square, triangle, square, triangle, ...
Draw the next two shapes: red circle, blue circle, red circle, ...
independent: Draw a pattern with two shapes across your page.
Make a colour pattern with three colours, such as red, yellow, blue, red, yellow, blue.
exit: Say what comes next: star, heart, star, heart, ...
lessons.homework: Find one pattern at home, such as stripes on a cushion, and draw it.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-draw the shapes and children colour them; EAL: chant the pattern aloud; stretch: make a three-part pattern (ABC).
